elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered still provides that the Agreement "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" with no mutual-written-agreement requirement, and the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied (opt-out is 60 days, not 30; no vendor reminder).

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal is "for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — a 12-month renewal term, retained unchanged.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires "sixty (60) days written notice"; 60 > 30, so the preferred opt-out threshold is not reached. Drafter must change the figure to thirty (30) days to satisfy this element.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears in the operative text; the 60-day pre-renewal reminder is only mentioned in the margin comment as our unpressed preferred position, which is not operative language.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the only pricing term (Section 3.1) is a fixed 30% share of Net Sales above the $11,000 monthly threshold, and Section 4.1 grants no renewal-time uplift right, so no price-increase cap is required.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 4.1 reads "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon sixty (60) days written notice to the other" — a 60-day window available to the Company (our client), exactly at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a regex artefact (the figure is written as "sixty (60)"); substantively the window is 60 days.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not triggered — Section 3.1 fixes consideration at 30% of Net Sales in excess of $11,000 per month and Section 4.1 contains no renewal price-uplift mechanic, so no cap language is needed.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the non-renewal/termination notice window is reduced from ninety (90) to sixty (60) days in operative text, and the price-uplift element is untriggered because the Agreement contains no renewal price-increase right (fixed 30% Net Sales share in Section 3.1).

Preferred level fails on three elements: renewal remains automatic without mutual written agreement, the opt-out notice is 60 rather than 30 days, and no 60-day vendor renewal reminder was inserted (it is only promised in the margin comment).

Minimality holds: the sole edit is the numeral change "ninety (90)" to "sixty (60)" within the existing sentence; no survival tails, procedures, or extra obligations were added, and the one-year renewal term and Termination Date definition are retained.

Intent preserved: the Effective Date trigger, one-year initial term, anniversary renewal mechanic, mutual notice structure, and the "Termination Date" definition all survive without contradiction or dangling references.

Observation (non-fatal, for drafter awareness): because the 90-day figure served as a mutual termination-for-convenience notice as well as the non-renewal exit, shortening it to 60 days also makes it easier for HDI to exit. If we want the benefit one-way, consider splitting the sentence into a Customer non-renewal right (≤60 days, or 30 days at preferred) and a separate vendor notice period; as drafted this remains within the fallback checklist and is not a defect.
